metadata.case_name: SIU LEUNG SING v. WONG FOOK WING AND ANOTHER

injuries.description: severe head injuries with consequent permanent disability.
source: suffered severe head injuries with consequent permanent disability.

manifestations.description: Speech and cognitive skills having been seriously affected.
Had not had any epileptic seizures since June/July 1997, being on regular anti-consultant therapy.

Diplopia (double vision); left eye is in a higher position than the right; can control diplopia by tilting his head to the right; needs to wear an optical lens with a correction in the left lens and adopt an abnormal head posture to compensate fully for the binocular diplopia.

Can wash, dress and feed himself but is substantially aided/assisted for shopping, travelling on only a few routes, requires assistance at the bank and is dependent to a substantial extent on members of his family and others.

source: The head injury required a craniotomy, and tracheostomy was later performed.
The head injury required a craniotomy, and tracheostomy was later performed.

treatments_received.treatment: Surgery to improve diplopia and head posture
source: He also underwent surgery to improve his diplopia and head posture.
He was in hospitals and rehabilitation units for almost nine months.
Ms Polina Chan of the Polina Chan Speech Therapy Centre had in June 1999 before he was seen by Dr Woo, recommended an extended period of speech therapy
it was not until November 2001 two years after Dr Woo's assessment that a three month course was commenced.
he had not had any epileptic seizures since June/July 1997, being on regular anti-consultant therapy.
Speech therapy is justified to maintain and consolidate progress. I will allow this in the sum of $300,000.00.
Applying the 20 year multiplier to the balance of the period for consultations (in net terms, 16) and to the drug costs, the total should be $46,400.00.

losses.description: There is no realistic prospect of his obtaining gainful employment. I approach this head of damage as a full loss.
He is dependent to a substantial extent, and permanently, on members of his family, and others in a variety of ways.

losses.category: Loss of ability to do domestic tasks
losses.description: He needs help with shopping, cooking, cleaning and washing; part-time help of 3 hours daily 7 days a week is necessary.
Permanent difficulties in using normal speech and language for daily communication; substantial deficits remained despite improvement after speech therapy.
Poor memory and comprehension; cognitive skills having been seriously affected for some time.
